newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: RABOBANK, FRANCE TELECOM MIGHT BID FOR TEL. LICENCE.
newsitem.headline: RABOBANK, FRANCE TELECOM MIGHT BID FOR TEL. LICENCE.

text.p: Dutch cooperative bank Rabobank and France Telecom said on Thursday they will investigate the possibility of a joint bid for a new mobile telephone licence in the Netherlands.
The licence will be auctioned later this year by the Dutch Ministry of telecommunications.
"Both Rabobank and France Telecom have the opinion that there are still ample opportunities for other mobile providers in the Dutch market," Rabobank said in a statement.
Last November the Dutch Ministry of telecommunications said it planned during 1997 to auction a licence for a DCS 1800 digital mobile phone network.

France Telecom is already active with mobile telephony in Argentina, Belgium, China, Greece, India, Japan, Lebanon, Poland, Mexico, Romania and Slovakia and more recently in Denmark with a DCS 1800-licence.
Dutch KPN and Libertel are currently the only mobile service providers in the Netherlands.
